name: Pisgah
overview: Pisgah is a significant location in the wilderness journey of Israel, serving as a vantage point from which Moses viewed the Promised Land. It is described as a hill or summit, such as in Numbers 21:20, marking a boundary of the land assigned to the Reubenites and Gadites. Additionally, Pisgah is the site where Balaam was taken by Balak to offer sacrifices and prophesy, as detailed in Numbers 23:13-17, highlighting its role as a place of divine encounter and revelation. These passages emphasize Pisgah not only as a geographical landmark but also as a place where God's purposes and promises were revealed to His people.
